anchors.paper_title: Single neurons in the human substantia nigra encode social learning signals
anchors.reason: The candidate is the preprint of the same study. The dataset README names this figshare release (29082671) with the same title and authors, recorded in the substantia nigra and globus pallidus during an ultimatum game.

metadata.methods_description: Alpha Omega wideband RAW streams (microelectrode tip and macro contact, 44 kHz) were recorded intraoperatively during a social exchange game. Int16 counts were scaled to microvolts and written as BrainVision float32 files. TTL digital-input edges were converted to events.tsv. Side, track and depth for each run were derived from Alpha Omega file names.

citation_details.title: In vitro analysis of expression vectors for DNA vaccination of horses: the effect of a Kozak sequence
citation_details.author: Guðbjörg Ásta Ólafsdóttir, Vilhjálmur Svansson, Sigurður Ingvarsson, Eliane Marti, Sigurbjörg Torsteinsdóttir
citation_details.abstract: One of the prerequisite for developing DNA vaccines for horses are vectors that are efficiently expressed in horse cells. We have analysed the ectopic expression of the human serum albumin gene in primary horse cells from different tissues. The vectors used are of pcDNA and pUC origin and include the cytomegalovirus (CMV) promoter. The pUC vectors contain CMV intron A whereas the pcDNA vectors do not. Insertion of intron A diminished the expression from the pcDNA vectors whereas insertion of a Kozak sequence upstream of the gene in two types of pUC vectors increased significantly the in vitro expression in primary horse cells derived from skin, lung, duodenum and kidney. We report for the first time the significance of full consensus Kozak sequences for protein expression in horse cells in vitro.
